source.scope: Source-aligned arguments for incomplete and consistent_unprovable. The first expands the self-substitution proof. The second expands the generic provability argument and its arithmetic instantiation.

nodes.name: Code refutation after substitution
nodes.lean:
let D : ℕ → Prop := fun φ : ℕ ↦
    IsSemiformula ℒₒᵣ 1 φ ∧ T.Provable (neg ℒₒᵣ <| subst ℒₒᵣ ?[numeral φ] φ)
  have D_re : REPred D := by
    have : 𝚺₁-Predicate fun φ : ℕ ↦
        IsSemiformula ℒₒᵣ 1 φ ∧ T.Provable (neg ℒₒᵣ <| subst ℒₒᵣ ?[numeral φ] φ) := by
      definability
    exact re_iff_sigma1.mpr this
  have D_spec (φ : Semisentence ℒₒᵣ 1) : D ⌜φ⌝ ↔ T ⊢ ∼φ/[⌜φ⌝] := by
    simp [D, ←provable_iff_provable, Sentence.quote_def,
      Rewriting.emb_subst_eq_subst_coe₁, Semiformula.quote_def]

nodes.name: Show D is recursively enumerable
nodes.lean:
have D_re : REPred D := by
    have : 𝚺₁-Predicate fun φ : ℕ ↦
        IsSemiformula ℒₒᵣ 1 φ ∧ T.Provable (neg ℒₒᵣ <| subst ℒₒᵣ ?[numeral φ] φ) := by
      definability
    exact re_iff_sigma1.mpr this

nodes.name: Represent D by a formula
nodes.lean:
let δ : Semisentence ℒₒᵣ 1 := codeOfREPred D
  have (n : ℕ) : D n ↔ T ⊢ δ/[↑n] := by
    simpa [Semiformula.coe_subst_eq_subst_coe₁] using re_complete D_re

nodes.name: Substitute δ’s own code
nodes.lean:
let π : Sentence ℒₒᵣ := δ/[⌜δ⌝]
  have : T ⊢ π ↔ T ⊢ ∼π := calc
    T ⊢ π ↔ T ⊢ δ/[⌜δ⌝]  := by rfl
    _     ↔ D ⌜δ⌝        := by simpa using (this ⌜δ⌝).symm
    _     ↔ T ⊢ ∼δ/[⌜δ⌝] := D_spec δ
    _     ↔ T ⊢ ∼π       := by rfl

refine incomplete_def.mpr ⟨π, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro h
    exact not_consistent_iff_inconsistent.mpr

  · intro h

nodes.name: Form standard provability
nodes.lean:
/-- The derivability condition D1. -/
theorem provable_D1 {σ} : T ⊢ σ → 𝗜𝚺₁ ⊢ □σ := fun h ↦
  provable_of_models _ _ fun (V : Type) _ _ ↦ by simpa [models_iff] using internalize_provability (V := V) h

/-- The derivability condition D2. -/
theorem provable_D2 {σ π} : 𝗜𝚺₁ ⊢ □(σ ➝ π) ➝ □σ ➝ □π :=
  provable_of_models _ _ fun (V : Type) _ _ ↦ by simpa [models_iff] using modus_ponens_sentence T

variable (T)

noncomputable abbrev _root_.LO.FirstOrder.Theory.standardProvability : Provability 𝗜𝚺₁ T where
  prov := T.provable
  D1 := provable_D1

variable {T}

instance : T.standardProvability.HBL2 := ⟨fun _ _ ↦ provable_D2⟩

lemma standardProvability_def (σ : Sentence L) : T.standardProvability σ = T.provabilityPred σ := rfl

instance [T.Δ₁] : T.standardProvability.SoundOnModel ℕ :=
  ⟨fun {σ} ↦ by simp [Arithmetic.standardProvability_def, models_iff]⟩

nodes.name: Supply derivability conditions
nodes.lean:
simpa [models_iff] using Bootstrapping.Arithmetic.sigma_one_complete (T := T) (V := V) hσ

/-- The derivability condition D3. -/
theorem provable_D3 [𝗣𝗔⁻ ⪯ T] {σ : Sentence ℒₒᵣ} :
    𝗜𝚺₁ ⊢ □σ ➝ □□σ := provable_sigma_one_complete (by simp)

open LO.Entailment LO.Entailment.FiniteContext

variable {U : ArithmeticTheory}

lemma provable_D2_context [𝗜𝚺₁ ⪯ U] {Γ σ π} (hσπ : Γ ⊢[U] □(σ ➝ π)) (hσ : Γ ⊢[U] □σ) :
    Γ ⊢[U] □π := FiniteContext.of'! (weakening inferInstance provable_D2) ⨀! hσπ ⨀! hσ

lemma provable_D3_context [𝗣𝗔⁻ ⪯ T] [𝗜𝚺₁ ⪯ U] {Γ σ} (hσπ : Γ ⊢[U] □σ) :
  Γ ⊢[U] □□σ := FiniteContext.of'! (weakening inferInstance provable_D3) ⨀! hσπ

lemma provable_sound [U.SoundOnHierarchy 𝚺 1] {σ} : U ⊢ □σ → T ⊢ σ := fun h ↦ by
  have : ℕ ⊧ₘ T.provabilityPred σ := ArithmeticTheory.SoundOn.sound (F := Arithmetic.Hierarchy 𝚺 1) h (by simp)
  simpa [models_iff] using this

lemma provable_complete [U.SoundOnHierarchy 𝚺 1] [𝗜𝚺₁ ⪯ U] {σ} : T ⊢ σ ↔ U ⊢ □σ :=
  ⟨fun h ↦ weakening inferInstance (provable_D1 h), provable_sound⟩

instance [𝗣𝗔⁻ ⪯ T] : T.standardProvability.HBL3 := ⟨fun _ ↦ provable_D3⟩

instance [𝗣𝗔⁻ ⪯ T] : T.standardProvability.HBL where

nodes.name: Diagonalize the provability predicate
Rule out a proof of G
nodes.lean:
variable [L.DecidableEq] [L.ReferenceableBy L] {T₀ T : Theory L} [T₀ ⪯ T] [Diagonalization T₀] [Consistent T]

variable (𝔅 : Provability T₀ T)

local notation "𝗚" => 𝔅.gödel

theorem unprovable_gödel : T ⊬ 𝗚 := by
  intro h;
  have h₁ : T ⊢ 𝔅 𝗚 := D1_shift h
  have : T ⊢ ⊥ := by cl_prover [h₁, 𝔅.gödel_spec, h]
  have : ¬Consistent T := not_consistent_iff_inconsistent.mpr <|
    inconsistent_iff_provable_bot.mpr this
  contradiction

nodes.name: Formalize the implication
nodes.lean:
/-- Formalized First Incompleteness Theorem -/
theorem formalized_unprovable_gödel : T₀ ⊢ 𝔅.con ➝ ∼𝔅 𝗚 := by
  suffices T₀ ⊢ ∼𝔅 ⊥ ➝ ∼𝔅 𝗚 from this
  have h₁ : T₀ ⊢ 𝔅 𝗚 ➝ 𝔅 (𝔅 𝗚) := 𝔅.D3 𝗚
  have h₂ : T₀ ⊢ 𝔅 𝗚 ➝ 𝔅 (𝔅 𝗚 ➝ ⊥) := prov_distribute_imply <| by cl_prover [𝔅.gödel_spec]
  have h₃ : T₀ ⊢ 𝔅 (𝔅 𝗚 ➝ ⊥) ➝ 𝔅 (𝔅 𝗚) ➝ 𝔅 ⊥ := 𝔅.D2 (𝔅 𝗚) ⊥
  cl_prover [h₁, h₂, h₃]

nodes.name: Relate G to consistency
nodes.lean:
lemma formalized_consistent_of_existance_unprovable (σ) : T₀ ⊢ ∼𝔅 σ ➝ 𝔅.con := contra! $ 𝔅.D2 _ _ ⨀ (𝔅.D1 efq!)

variable [T₀ ⪯ T] [Diagonalization T₀] (𝔅)

local notation "𝗚" => 𝔅.gödel

/-- Formalized First Incompleteness Theorem -/
theorem formalized_unprovable_gödel : T₀ ⊢ 𝔅.con ➝ ∼𝔅 𝗚 := by
  suffices T₀ ⊢ ∼𝔅 ⊥ ➝ ∼𝔅 𝗚 from this
  have h₁ : T₀ ⊢ 𝔅 𝗚 ➝ 𝔅 (𝔅 𝗚) := 𝔅.D3 𝗚
  have h₂ : T₀ ⊢ 𝔅 𝗚 ➝ 𝔅 (𝔅 𝗚 ➝ ⊥) := prov_distribute_imply <| by cl_prover [𝔅.gödel_spec]
  have h₃ : T₀ ⊢ 𝔅 (𝔅 𝗚 ➝ ⊥) ➝ 𝔅 (𝔅 𝗚) ➝ 𝔅 ⊥ := 𝔅.D2 (𝔅 𝗚) ⊥
  cl_prover [h₁, h₂, h₃]

theorem gödel_iff_con : T₀ ⊢ 𝗚 ⭤ 𝔅.con := by
  have h₁ : T₀ ⊢ ∼𝔅 𝗚 ➝ 𝔅.con := formalized_consistent_of_existance_unprovable 𝗚
  have h₂ : T₀ ⊢ 𝔅.con ➝ ∼𝔅 𝗚 := 𝔅.formalized_unprovable_gödel
  have h₃ : T₀ ⊢ 𝗚 ⭤ ∼𝔅 𝗚 := 𝔅.gödel_spec
  cl_prover [h₁, h₂, h₃]

nodes.name: Reduce a proof of consistency to G
nodes.lean:
theorem con_unprovable [Consistent T] : T ⊬ 𝔅.con := by
  intro h
  have : T₀ ⊢ 𝗚 ⭤ 𝔅.con := 𝔅.gödel_iff_con
  have : T ⊢ 𝗚 := by cl_prover [h, this]
  exact 𝔅.unprovable_gödel this

lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.incomplete.title: First incompleteness theorem
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.incomplete.summary: A Σ₁-sound arithmetic theory with a Δ₁ presentation that extends R₀ leaves some sentence undecided. The proof constructs a sentence for which a proof of either side would give a proof of the other side, contradicting consistency.
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.incomplete.statement_latex:
ext{If }T	ext{ is an arithmetic theory with a }\Delta_1	ext{ presentation, }R_0\preceq T,	ext{ and }T	ext{ is }\Sigma_1	ext{-sound, then }\exists\varphi\in\operatorname{Sent}(\mathcal L_{\mathrm A})\; igl(T
vdash\varphi\ \land\ T
vdash
eg\varphi igr).
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.incomplete.why_here: The constructed sentence supplies the witness required by the theorem.

lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.consistent.title: Second incompleteness theorem
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.consistent.summary: In the arithmetic setting of the graph, a consistent theory cannot prove its standard arithmetical consistency sentence. The result applies the generic provability theorem to the standard predicate for proofs in the given theory.
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.consistent.statement_latex:
ext{Let }T	ext{ be an arithmetic theory with a }\Delta_1	ext{ presentation and }I\Sigma_1\preceq T.	ext{ If }T
vdash ot,	ext{ then }T
vdash\operatorname{Con}(T),\quad \operatorname{Con}(T):=
eg\operatorname{Pr}_T(\ulcorner ot\urcorner),	ext{ where }\operatorname{Pr}_T	ext{ is standard arithmetical provability for }T.
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.consistent.why_here: The final edge specializes the generic result to arithmetic provability and the arithmetic consistency sentence.

lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.re_iff_sig.title: Σ₁ Definability and Recursive Enumerability
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.re_iff_sig.summary: A predicate on natural numbers is recursively enumerable exactly when it is Σ₁-definable. Here the direction from definability to enumerability is used.
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.re_iff_sig.why_here: It converts the definability calculation for D into recursive enumerability.

lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.re_complet.title: Representability of Recursively Enumerable Predicates
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.re_complet.summary: In the setting of the first proof, an enumerable predicate has a representing formula whose numeral instances are provable precisely for numbers in the predicate.
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.re_complet.why_here: It supplies the general result used to choose the particular formula δ for D.

lean:LO.FirstOrder.Theory.standardProvab.title: Standard Provability Predicate
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Theory.standardProvab.summary: The standard provability structure pairs the arithmetical predicate for proofs in T with the rule that an actual T-proof yields an IΣ₁-proof of the corresponding provability assertion.
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Theory.standardProvab.why_here: The arithmetic construction unfolds this definition.

lean:LO.FirstOrder.Theory.consistent.title: Arithmetical Consistency Sentence
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Theory.consistent.summary: The Π₁ sentence for consistency states that the code of absurdity has no T-proof according to the standard provability predicate.
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Theory.consistent.why_here: Unfolding the definition identifies the sentence to which the arithmetic conclusion applies.

lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.provable_D.title: Third Derivability Condition
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.provable_D.summary: Under the hypothesis that T extends PA⁻, IΣ₁ proves that provability in T implies provability in T of that very provability assertion.
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.provable_D.statement_latex: \text{If }\mathrm{PA}^{-}\preceq T,\text{ then for each arithmetic sentence }\sigma,\quad I\Sigma_1\vdash\Box_T\sigma\to\Box_T\Box_T\sigma,\qquad \Box_T\theta:=\operatorname{Pr}_T(\ulcorner\theta\urcorner).
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.provable_D.why_here: The derivability step includes this condition, which lets the internal argument reason about iterated provability.

lean:LO.ProvabilityLogic.Provability.göd.title: Gödel Sentence Fixed-Point Equation
lean:LO.ProvabilityLogic.Provability.göd.summary: For a provability predicate B for T and a base theory T₀ admitting diagonalization, the associated Gödel sentence is provably equivalent in T₀ to the assertion of its own unprovability.
lean:LO.ProvabilityLogic.Provability.göd.why_here: The diagonalization step summarizes this specification.

lean:LO.ProvabilityLogic.Provability.con.title: Abstract Second Incompleteness Theorem
lean:LO.ProvabilityLogic.Provability.con.summary: With diagonalization in the base theory, transfer to T, and the derivability conditions for B, consistency of T rules out a T-proof of the sentence that denies B-provability of absurdity.
lean:LO.ProvabilityLogic.Provability.con.why_here: The generic proof step summarizes this theorem before its arithmetic specialization.

fact:presentation.title: Δ₁ Presentation
fact:presentation.summary: The theory’s presentation supplies definability information about its axioms for reasoning about coded proofs.
fact:presentation.why_here: It is part of the setting for the coded refutation predicate and the arithmetic provability structure.

fact:r0.title: Extension of R₀
fact:r0.summary: The arithmetic theory T extends the base theory R₀.
fact:r0.why_here: The extension provides the arithmetic base used to represent D by provability.

fact:soundness.title: Σ₁ Soundness
fact:soundness.summary: Every Σ₁ sentence proved by T is true in the standard natural numbers. An inconsistent theory would prove false Σ₁ sentences, so this hypothesis implies consistency.
fact:soundness.why_here: Consistency is what rules out simultaneous proofs of the constructed sentence and its negation.

fact:isigma.title: Arithmetic Base IΣ₁
fact:isigma.summary: IΣ₁ is arithmetic with induction for Σ₁ formulas. It serves as the base in which the arithmetic provability conditions and the fixed-point equivalence are proved.
fact:isigma.why_here: It supplies the base theory for the arithmetic instances of these constructions.

fact:consistency.title: External Consistency
fact:consistency.summary: The assumption is that there exists no T-proof of absurdity.
fact:consistency.why_here: It rules out the actual T-proof of absurdity that would follow from a proof of the Gödel sentence.

step:define-D.title: Code Self-Substitution and Refutation
step:define-D.summary: Take a natural number n and check whether it codes a formula with one free variable. For a valid code, substitute the numeral for n into that formula, negate the resulting sentence, and ask whether T proves it. This defines D and gives its interpretation on actual formula codes.
step:define-D.why_here: It creates the predicate that will be represented and then evaluated at its representing formula’s own code.

fact:define-D.title: Coded Refutation Predicate
fact:define-D.summary: On the code of a one-variable formula, D asserts that T proves the negation of the sentence obtained by substituting that code’s numeral into the formula.
fact:define-D.why_here: This description supports both the definability calculation and the later evaluation at the code of δ.

step:enumerate-D.title: Σ₁ Definability Gives Enumerability
step:enumerate-D.summary: The coded formula test, substitution, and provability condition in D together give a Σ₁ definition. The equivalence between Σ₁ definability and recursive enumerability then gives that D is recursively enumerable.
step:enumerate-D.why_here: It establishes the hypothesis needed to represent D.

fact:enumerate-D.title: Recursive Enumerability of D
fact:enumerate-D.summary: The numbers satisfying D form a recursively enumerable set.
fact:enumerate-D.why_here: This is the input to the representability theorem.

step:represent-D.title: Representability Theorem
step:represent-D.summary: Apply representability to the recursively enumerable predicate D in the theory extending R₀. This provides a particular formula δ whose instance at the numeral for n is provable in T exactly when D holds of n.
step:represent-D.why_here: It supplies both the formula for self-substitution and the equivalence used at its code.

fact:represent-D.title: Representing Formula δ
fact:represent-D.summary: The formula δ chosen for D satisfies an equivalence about T-proofs for every numeral instance.
fact:represent-D.why_here: The next step uses the instance with n equal to the code of δ.

step:self-substitute.title: Substitute δ’s Own Code
step:self-substitute.summary: Set π to the instance of δ at the numeral for its own code. Representability identifies a proof of π with D holding of that code, and the definition of D identifies the same condition with a proof of ¬π. This gives an equivalence between the two external provability claims.
step:self-substitute.why_here: It ties proofs of the two opposite sentences to the same predicate value.

fact:self-substitute.title: Equivalent Proof Claims
fact:self-substitute.summary: For this particular π, a T-proof of π exists exactly when a T-proof of its negation exists.
fact:self-substitute.why_here: Either proposed proof forces the opposite proof in the final contradiction.

step:exclude-both.title: Exclude Both Proofs by Consistency
step:exclude-both.summary: Assume T proves π or assume it proves ¬π. In each case the equivalence supplies a proof of the opposite sentence, so T would prove absurdity, contrary to the consistency supplied by Σ₁ soundness. Thus π witnesses incompleteness.
step:exclude-both.why_here: It turns the equivalence of proof claims into failure of both claims.

fact:exclude-both.title: Undecided Sentence π
fact:exclude-both.summary: The particular sentence obtained by substituting δ’s own code into δ has neither a proof nor a refutation in T.
fact:exclude-both.why_here: This local witness establishes the existential conclusion of the first theorem.

step:standard-provability.title: Construct Standard Provability
step:standard-provability.summary: Use T’s coded proof predicate as the arithmetic provability predicate. An actual T-proof yields an IΣ₁-proof of the corresponding provability sentence by D1. The formalized combination of proofs by modus ponens supplies D2 over the same base.
step:standard-provability.why_here: It furnishes the arithmetic provability structure used in the second theorem.

fact:standard-provability.title: Arithmetic Provability Structure
fact:standard-provability.summary: For the given arithmetic theory T, the standard structure uses the coded proof predicate and works over IΣ₁.
fact:standard-provability.why_here: It supplies the predicate used in the derivability conditions, consistency sentence, and arithmetic Gödel sentence.

step:hbl-conditions.title: Hilbert–Bernays–Löb Derivability Conditions
step:hbl-conditions.summary: Start with standard provability and the previously supplied D1 and D2. With PA⁻ contained in T, formalized Σ₁ completeness applies to the Σ₁ assertion that T proves σ, giving D3. This completes the derivability conditions used in the internal argument.
step:hbl-conditions.why_here: It supplies the iteration and proof-combination rules needed to derive internal provability of absurdity.

fact:hbl-conditions.title: Derivability Conditions for Standard Provability
fact:hbl-conditions.summary: The arithmetic instance has D1 for internalizing proofs, D2 for combining internalized implications with their premises, and D3 for iterating provability.
fact:hbl-conditions.why_here: The internal proof uses these conditions to work with assertions about proofs inside the base theory.

step:consistency-sentence.title: Define the Consistency Sentence
step:consistency-sentence.summary: Apply the standard provability predicate to the code of absurdity and negate the result. The resulting Π₁ sentence holds in a model exactly when the model satisfies the corresponding coded consistency assertion.
step:consistency-sentence.why_here: It identifies the arithmetic sentence whose unprovability is at issue.

fact:consistency-sentence.title: Internal Consistency of T
fact:consistency-sentence.summary: Con(T) is the arithmetic sentence asserting that there is no coded T-proof of absurdity.
fact:consistency-sentence.why_here: Its abstract counterpart is the antecedent of the internal unprovability implication.

step:godel-sentence.title: Diagonal Lemma
step:godel-sentence.summary: Apply the diagonal lemma over the base theory T₀ to the one-variable formula denying B-provability of the sentence coded by its input. It gives a sentence G such that T₀ proves G equivalent to the denial of B-provability of G itself.
step:godel-sentence.why_here: The fixed-point equivalence is used in both the external and the internal unprovability arguments.

fact:godel-sentence.title: Fixed-Point Equivalence for G
fact:godel-sentence.summary: The base theory proves the fixed-point equivalence for the particular Gödel sentence associated with B. Here □ denotes the sentence asserting B-provability of its argument.
fact:godel-sentence.why_here: It supplies the negated provability assertion used in each argument involving G.

step:godel-unprovable.title: External Unprovability of the Gödel Sentence
step:godel-unprovable.summary: Suppose T proves G. D1 gives a proof in the base of the assertion that G is provable, which transfers to T. The fixed-point equivalence also transfers to T and lets T derive the denial of that assertion from G. This gives an actual proof of absurdity, contradicting the external consistency assumption.
step:godel-unprovable.why_here: It supplies the contradiction used if a proof of consistency is converted into a proof of G.

fact:godel-unprovable.title: No T-Proof of G
fact:godel-unprovable.summary: Under the external consistency assumption and the given base-theory setup, there is no proof of the chosen Gödel sentence in T.
fact:godel-unprovable.why_here: It eliminates the proof of G obtained from the hypothetical consistency proof.

step:internal-unprovability.title: Formalized First Incompleteness Theorem
step:internal-unprovability.summary: Work in T₀ and write □ for B-provability. From □G, D3 gives □□G, and internalizing the fixed-point consequence that G implies ¬□G gives □(□G → ⊥). D2 combines these to give □⊥. Contraposition yields the internal implication from consistency to ¬□G.
step:internal-unprovability.why_here: It supplies the direction from internal consistency to the right side of the fixed-point equivalence.

fact:internal-unprovability.title: Consistency Implies Internal Unprovability
fact:internal-unprovability.summary: The base theory proves that the consistency sentence for B implies the sentence denying B-provability of G.
fact:internal-unprovability.why_here: This implication is one direction of the equivalence between internal consistency and ¬□G.

step:equate-godel-consistency.title: Gödel Sentence–Consistency Equivalence
step:equate-godel-consistency.summary: The formalized first theorem gives consistency implying ¬□G in T₀. For the reverse, a proof of absurdity would yield a proof of G by internalizing the implication from absurdity to G and applying D2, so ¬□G implies consistency. The fixed-point equivalence then replaces ¬□G with G.
step:equate-godel-consistency.why_here: It gives the implication from consistency to G that can be transferred to T.

fact:equate-godel-consistency.title: G Equivalent to Internal Consistency
fact:equate-godel-consistency.summary: The base theory proves that G and the consistency sentence for B are equivalent.
fact:equate-godel-consistency.why_here: It allows a hypothetical T-proof of the consistency sentence to be converted into a T-proof of G.

step:generic-unprovability.title: Second Incompleteness Theorem
step:generic-unprovability.summary: Suppose T proves the consistency sentence for B. Transfer the base theory’s equivalence between that sentence and G to T, and apply the direction from consistency to G. The resulting T-proof of G contradicts the external unprovability result.
step:generic-unprovability.why_here: It proves the generic result used with standard provability in the arithmetic theorem.

fact:generic-unprovability.title: Unprovability of the Generic Consistency Sentence
fact:generic-unprovability.summary: For the abstract provability predicate B in the stated setup, consistency of T rules out a T-proof of the sentence denying B-provability of absurdity.
fact:generic-unprovability.why_here: The arithmetic root takes B to be T’s standard provability predicate.

concepts.title: Recursive Enumerability and Representability
concepts.summary: A recursively enumerable predicate admits a search that eventually confirms every positive instance. Representability here turns membership into provability of the corresponding numeral instance of a formula.

concepts.title: Gödel Coding and Diagonalization
concepts.summary: An arithmetical formula can take the numeral for a formula’s code as input. Using its own code yields a self-substitution instance, and the diagonal lemma uses coding to obtain a sentence with a provable fixed-point equivalence.

concepts.title: Arithmetized Provability
concepts.summary: The expression □σ abbreviates a sentence asserting that the code of σ has a proof according to the chosen predicate. The judgment T ⊢ σ asserts, in the metatheory, that a T-proof exists.

concepts.title: Hilbert–Bernays–Löb Conditions
concepts.summary: D1 makes actual proofs yield provable assertions of provability. D2 formalizes modus ponens for those assertions, and D3 says that a provability assertion implies its own provability.

concepts.title: Soundness and Consistency
concepts.summary: External consistency means that the theory has no proof of absurdity. Σ₁ soundness implies this because an inconsistent theory proves false Σ₁ sentences. The internal consistency sentence expresses the absence of a proof of absurdity using an arithmetical proof predicate.
